hints: If a or b is the forbidden city, the answer is NO.
A non-articulation city cannot disconnect the remaining cities.
Represent articulation points and biconnected blocks as a tree.
analogy: Replace each robust district with one block and use junction cities to connect the blocks.
example: For roads 1-2-3, removing 2 disconnects 1 from 3, while removing 1 does not disconnect 2 from 3.
algorithm: Use a DFS low-link algorithm with an edge stack to find all biconnected blocks. Build the block-cut tree with one node per block and one node per articulation vertex, joining each block to its articulation vertices. Map every non-articulation original vertex to its unique block and every articulation vertex to its own tree node. Preprocess depths and LCA. For each query, reject if c equals a or b; otherwise answer NO exactly when c is an articulation vertex and its block-cut node lies on the path between the mapped nodes of a and b. Test path membership using tree distances.
correctness: The block-cut tree captures every way components meet: deleting an articulation vertex separates exactly the branches incident to its node. Thus the deletion disconnects a and b exactly when that node lies on their unique tree path. Deleting any other vertex leaves the rest connected.
complexity: For n cities, m roads and q queries, decomposition takes O(n+m), LCA preprocessing O((n+m) log n), and queries O(q log n); space is O((n+m) log n).
